newsitem.title: FRANCE: SOCCER-FRENCH CHAMPIONS PLAGUED BY INJURIES.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-FRENCH CHAMPIONS PLAGUED BY INJURIES.

text.p: Auxerre have a foot in the door of the European Cup quarter-finals despite injury woes that have played havoc with their chances of a successful defence of their French first division title.
Defeat at home by Bastia at the weekend has left Auxerre seventh, 10 points adrift of leaders Paris Saint-Germain after taking only one point from their last four matches.
"Against Bastia, we fought hard, but on a playing level the team is changing too often," said coach Guy Roux.
"If I had a month to give the team its shape, I'd get there. But now we're playing every three days. It's very, very worrying for the coming fortnight."

Auxerre are away to Lille on Friday, then meet Glasgow Rangers at home in their final champions' league group A match on December 4 when a draw will see them through to the European Cup quarter-finals.
Three days later they have a tough home game against Jean-Pierre Papin's Bordeaux, who have scored 11 goals in their last three games, including six away.
What will particularly concern Roux ahead of Rangers' visit is that Auxerre have lost their last two home games after being in front.

Their efforts in a shock 2-1 victory away to Ajax Amsterdam last week left them without injury victims Bernard Diomede up front, Christian Henna in midfield and Philippe Charbonnier in goal for the Bastia match.
Fifteen minutes into the match, left back Eric Assati, one of several second choice players who shone in Amsterdam had to come off with an injury.
French international defender Alain Goma, suspended for the Amsterdam match, played in a makeshift midfield in which only Algeria's Moussa Saib was a regular.
Saib, referring to Auxerre's domestic slump, said: "It's the cadence of a relegation candidate. But then, last year we were 10 points behind PSG."

Captain Sabri Lamouchi has been out with an ankle injury since Auxerre beat Grasshopper Zurich in their last champions' league match at home on October 16, though like Australian defender Ned Zelic -- out since mid-September -- he is nearing recovery.
